{{Quote|Slavery is the natural order of things. The weak deserve nothing more than to kneel before the strong, bound to our service.|Queen Miraj Scintel|audio=Zygerrian2.flac|<ref name="SOTR" />}}
The '''Zygerrians''' were a [[humanoid]] [[feline]] [[species]]<ref name="Survival Skills" /> from [[Zygerria]].<ref name="Zygerria" /> Having evolved from a horned [[Zygerrian precursor species|sentient canine species]],<ref name="Falcon 91">{{BuildFalconCite|91|Guide to the Galaxy}}</ref> they built a powerful [[Zygerrian Slave Empire|empire]] by capturing and selling [[Slavery|slaves]] until the [[Jedi]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] went to [[Jedi–Zygerrian conflict|war]] with them and outlawed it. The Zygerrians openly revived their slave trade when they allied with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the [[Clone Wars]].

==History==
===Height of power===
{{Quote|For thousands of years, Zygerria supplied slave labor to the galaxy. We prospered. Our customers prospered. Then the Jedi came.|Darts D'Nar|<ref name="Kidnapped" />}}
[[File:DartsDNar-TCWCEJtB.png|thumb|left|200px|Zygerrians favored cruel methods of control, like electro-whips.]]
The Zygerrians were a powerful people in the [[Standard day|days]] of the [[Galactic Republic|Old Republic]].<ref name="DB:Z">{{Databank|zygerrian|Zygerrian}}</ref> Their [[Zygerrian Slave Empire|empire]] provided [[Slavery|slave]] labor to [[the galaxy]] in which both the Zygerrians and their customers prospered.<ref name="Kidnapped" /> Eventually, the Zygerrian Empire came to dominate a large portion of the region, stretching from [[Argazda]] down the [[Salin Corridor]] [[Hyperspace route|hyperlane]]. The slavers were also in control of the [[Triellus Trade Route]], which provided access to the planet [[Ryloth]]. At the height of their empire, the Zygerrians provided slaves to other powerful factions operating in the region, such as the [[Hutt]]s and [[Chevin]] slavers.<ref name="Friends"/>
However, their slave trade was outlawed by the Old Republic. The [[Jedi]] [[Jedi Knight|Knights]] liberated countless slaves from the Zygerrians and [[Jedi–Zygerrian conflict|pushed]] their Empire into the underworld's shadows, resulting in many Zygerrians developing a seething hatred of the Jedi and their Order.<ref name="DB:Z" /> Despite the fall of their overall empire and the ensuing loss of much of their political influence,<ref name="Kidnapped" /> the Zygerrian slave trade continued<ref name="Tempest Runner">''[[The High Republic: Tempest Runner]]''</ref> in a reduced state. Much of the Zygerrians' wealth dried up with the collapse of their high-profile slave trade, however.<ref name="Kidnapped" />

During the [[High Republic Era]],<ref name="Tempest Runner" /> the tradition of Zygerrian slavery<ref name="Kidnapped" /> was covertly continued through the [[Zygerrian Alliance]], which publicly existed as a legitimate enterprise.<ref name="Tempest Runner" /> The [[Nihil]] marauders maintained relations with the Zygerrians during the era, such as by selling off [[prisoner]]s to the Zygerrians to make a profit.<ref name="Mission to Disaster">''[[The High Republic: Mission to Disaster]]''</ref> Around [[255 BBY]],<ref name="255 Date">{{HighRepublicShow|f0l-OuG3BVg|High Republic Phase II Deep Dive, Star Wars Celebration, and More!|sw_url=video/high-republic-phase-ii-deep-dive-star-wars-celebration-and-more}}</ref> the [[Jedi Order]] launched an [[Attack on the Zygerrian camp|attack]] on a Zygerrian camp to free everyone within. Among those rescued was a [[Twi'lek]] [[Gender|woman]] named [[Lourna Dee]], who would go onto join the Nihil and arise to the rank of [[Tempest Runner]].<ref name="Tempest Runner" /> When Tempest Runner [[Kara Xoo]]'s [[Kara Xoo's Tempest|Nihil Tempest]] kidnapped [[Youngling|children]] to recruit them into the ranks of the Nihil, Xoo had those who disobeyed during training sold off to the slavers, instilling fear in those who remained to help push them to accept the Nihil.<ref name="Mission to Disaster" />

===Rebuilding the slave trade===
====Clone Wars====
{{Quote|My queen is going to bring back the royal slave auction as in the days before the Jedi. Zygerria will be rich and powerful again.|Darts D'Nar|audio=Zygerrian7.flac|<ref name="Kidnapped" />}}
[[File:Zygerrians2-SWE.png|thumb|right|250px|Two Zygerrians in service to the Slave Empire]]
In the late Republic Era, the Zygerrians maintained slave-run work colonies,<ref name="TPM-25th">[[The Phantom Menace 25th Anniversary Special 1|''The Phantom Menace'' 25th Anniversary Special 1]]</ref> yet their empire still had not yet been truly reformed. During the [[Clone Wars]], Zygerria's [[queen]] [[Miraj Scintel]], formed an alliance with [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Confederate]] leader [[Count]] [[Dooku]] to finally rebuild her people's Slave Empire.<ref name="Kidnapped" />

She sent [[Commander]] [[Darts D'Nar]] to accompany Dooku, a tactical droid and their forces to occupy [[Kiros]]. Lead to believe by Dooku they would be brought to a safe place to wait out the war,<ref name="Kidnapped" /> the [[Togruta]] [[colonist]]s were then taken to [[Kadavo]]'s [[Kadavo slave processing facility|slave processing facility]]. However, the Republic and the Jedi would once again crack down on the Zygerrian enterprise by launching an [[Battle of Kadavo|attack]] on the facility, freeing the slaves and destroying their installation. Additionally, Dooku had killed Scintel for her disobedience, leaving [[Prime Minister]]<ref name="SOTR" /> [[Atai Molec]] to take her place as the empire's ruler.<ref name="Friends">''[[Friends Like These]]''</ref>

====Imperial Era====
{{Quote|With the meddling Republic gone, we can return to Kadavo and rebuild what was taken from us. Under this new empire, our operation will flourish once again.|Raney|<ref name="Rampage">{{TBB|Rampage (episode)}}</ref>}}
[[File:ZygerriansAreBack-TBB.png|thumb|left|300px|A group of Zygerrians operated on Ord Mantell after the Clone Wars.]]  
Despite their defeats during the Republic Era, the [[Imperial Era|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire]] saw new opportunities for the Zygerrians. A group of slavers led by [[Raney]] were established on [[Ord Mantell]] shortly after the end of the war.<ref name="Rampage" /> The Zygerrian [[MaDall]] also established an [[MaDall's empire|empire]] on the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] world of [[Oon]] during the Imperial Era. MaDall's operations were [[Mission to Oon|disrupted]] by the [[Mandalorian]] [[Sabine Wren]].<ref name="RSlavers" />

Following the [[Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY]], at least one Zygerrian slaver was based at an Imperial slave labor [[Mining|mine]] on the planet [[Sevarcos]]. During the [[Battle on Sevarcos]], the slaver tried to kill the [[Wookiee]] slave [[Greybok]] but was bludgeoned to death by the [[Weequay]] [[Hatchet]].<ref name="Afermath">[[Aftermath (novel)|''Aftermath'']]</ref>

===Under the New Republic===
During the [[New Republic Era]], the Zygerrians were still hopeful of rebuilding their slave trade, and benefited from the strain that the [[First Order]] had placed on the [[New Republic]].<ref name="Falcon 91" /> At some point, Zygerrian slavers captured the hulking [[Talz]] [[Ramakak]], but Ramakak was eventually rescued by the ruthless treasure hunter [[Zool Zendiat]]. As thanks, Ramakak joined the [[Zendiat Collective]] as his muscle.<ref name="Heroes of Galaxy">''[[Star Wars Adventures, Volume 1: Heroes of the Galaxy]]''</ref>

==Society and culture==
They were ruled by a [[monarchy]], who was served by the [[Prime Minister]] and the [[Zygerrian Royal Guard|Zygerrian royal guard]]. They patrolled on the backs of flying [[brezak]]s and brandished [[electro-whip]]s to control their slaves.<ref name="Slaves of the Republic">{{TCW|Slaves of the Republic}}</ref>

Zygerrians had furry, tufted [[ear]]s.<ref name="Join the Battle">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''</ref> Their ears inspired the [[hair]]style known as [[Zygerrian-style faux crests]]. The hairstyle was sported by [[Razoo Qin-Fee]], a [[Kanjiklub]]ber who once participated in the [[underworld Zygerrian fighting circuit]].<ref name="Ep. VII">''[[Star Wars: The Force Awakens: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> They lived in a rocky natural habitat.<ref name="VE" />

==Zygerrians in the galaxy==
[[File:TasiLowa-LostFound.png|thumb|right|250px|Jedi Padawan Tasi Lowa]]
Despite their acrimonious history with the Jedi,<ref name="Kidnapped" /> individual Zygerrians could be found within the Jedi Order's ranks over its history. [[Farzala Tarabal]]<ref name="THRA 1">[[The High Republic Adventures (2021) 1|''The High Republic Adventures'' (2021) 1]]</ref> and [[Tasi Lowa]] were Zygerrians who served the Order as Jedi during the High Republic Era.<ref name="L/F Trivia">{{SW|url=lost-found-trivia-gallery-the-acolyte|text="Lost / Found" Trivia Gallery | The Acolyte}} {{C|Slide 8}}</ref> Active during the later Republic Era, another Zygerrian Jedi was named [[Tosan]], who rose to the position of [[Jedi Master]].<ref name="AoR-Kenobi">[[Age of Republic - Obi-Wan Kenobi 1|''Age of Republic - Obi-Wan Kenobi'' 1]]</ref>

In a dream of the young enslaved Anakin Skywalker, he saw his mother [[Shmi Skywalker Lars|Shmi Skywalker]] and other enslaved individuals set to be shipped off to Zygerrian work colonies, only for him to appear—as a Jedi returning home with a yellow lightsaber<ref name="TPM-25th" />—and free them all. While Skywalker would indeed join the ranks of the Jedi Order,<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref> his mother would be freed from slavery at the hands of the [[Toydarian]] [[Watto]] thanks to the [[Lars family]],<ref name="Queen Hope">''[[Queen's Hope]]''</ref> although she would die in her son's arms when he finally returned to Tatooine.<ref name="ATOC">{{Film|II}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Zygerrian2.jpg|thumb|left|225px|The original Zygerrian design, as depicted in the Legends sourcebook ''[[Galaxy at War]]'']]
The Zygerrians were first mentioned in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity in the ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Bill Slavicsek]] and [[Curtis Smith]] and published in [[1987]].<ref name="SW Sourcebook">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> The species remained relatively untouched by the Expanded Universe until the [[2008]] [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' project]]. Writer [[Henry Gilroy]] originally developed a story outline involving the Zygerrians while working on the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''The Clone Wars'' television series]]. However, Gilroy's proposed story was deemed too complex for the series at that point, so it was not produced as episodes for the show.<ref name="Complete Season 4">{{HomeVideoCite|set=Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season Four|featurette=The Slaves of Zygerria}}</ref> Instead, Gilroy's story was realized as [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Slaves of the Republic|''Slaves of the Republic'']], a [[2008]] story arc of the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars (comic series)|''The Clone Wars'' comic series]]. Written by Gilroy and illustrated by [[Scott Hepburn]], this story tied into the television series.<ref name="Slaves 2">[[The Clone Wars 2|''The Clone Wars'' 2]]</ref> 

In [[2011]]–[[2012]], the ''Slaves of the Republic'' comic books were adapted into three episodes of the television series, titled "[[Kidnapped]]," "[[Slaves of the Republic]]," and "[[Escape from Kadavo]]." The episodes followed the same premise as the comics but featured a number of differences, most notably a visual redesign for the Zygerrians that conflicted with their previous depiction in both the comic series and the [[2009]] ''[[Galaxy at War]]'' sourcebook as resembling humans with pointed ears, long red hair and bony spurs on their forehead and chins. [[Dave Filoni]] felt this look was too close to a live-action TV show with limited makeup resources for aliens, and opted to blend them with a [[Wikipedia:coyote|coyote]]-like appearance, stating the coyote's [[Wikipedia:Coyote (mythology)|trickster]] reputation helped the Zygerrians look more cunning and deceitful.<ref name="Complete Season 4" />

Zygerrians first appeared in live-action<ref name="Collider">{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/the-acolyte-zygerrian-practical-effects-leslye-headland-comments|text='The Acolyte' Will Use Practical Effects for the Zygerrians Says Showrunner|author=Diego Peralta|date=2023-04-14|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]|quote=Oh, I got a Zygerrian in live-action, which that was one of my things. I was like, 'I've got to get a Zygerrian.' The poor makeup department. Let me tell you what I put them through. She's a blink-and-you’ll-miss-her in the teaser, actually. So I got her in there as a Padawan.|archivedate=20230718195621}}</ref> in the [[Lost / Found|first episode]] of the television series [[Star Wars: The Acolyte|''The Acolyte'']],<ref name="Lost / Found" /> which aired on [[June 4]], [[2024]].<ref name="Announcement">{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-teaser-poster|text=''The Acolyte'' Teaser Poster, Premiere Date Revealed}}</ref>
